name: Button
summary: Triggers an action. One component for text, icon and text, and icon-only buttons, at seven sizes, with two ways to show an operation in progress (three: inside, ring, fill). Not for navigation (use Link; `href` only for a destination that is the main call to action), on/off settings (use Switch), a menu of actions (use MenuButton) or one exclusive choice (use SegmentedControl).
a11y: Native `button`. Targets: 44 px and up from `normal`; `s` (36 px) and `xs` (24 px, the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum) are dense sizes for dense surfaces (O41). In progress keeps the same focused element, locked with `aria-disabled` and `aria-busy`, never `disabled`, and its present-tense label is the accessible name; the ring variant's arc is decorative (`aria-hidden`) and meets 3:1. The fill variant is a hidden `progressbar` with `aria-valuenow`, read as the button's description; its filled copy of the label is `aria-hidden`, and the label reaches 4.5:1 over both parts. Unavailable stays focusable with `aria-disabled` and its reason as the description. Icon-only buttons are named by `label`, which also shows as their hint (a Tooltip, hidden from assistive technology because it repeats the name; an unavailable button's hint is its reason, already its description). No native `title`, so there's one hint. A disclosure sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and shows open as a selected tint. Every label, pending and done alike, shares one box, so the width never changes. With `href` it is a native `a[href]` (Enter follows it) with the same look and focus ring; unavailable keeps it focusable with `aria-disabled`, its reason as the description, and stops it going.

props.name: label
props.description: A verb first, 3 words or fewer. Shown, or the accessible name of an icon-only button.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon; required when `iconOnly`.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description: Shows only the icon; `label` becomes its accessible name and its tooltip. Square at every size.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Shows the label of an icon-only button, or the reason of an unavailable one, as a Tooltip on hover and keyboard focus: one hint, never the browser's own `title`. On by default; `false` only where something next to it already shows the same words. An explicit Tooltip around the button replaces it (for a side or a shortcut).

props.name: emphasis
props.description: `primary` for the one main action in a view, `default` otherwise, `quiet` inside toolbars and other enclosed groups, `danger` for an action that destroys or can't be undone.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The action can't happen and there's nothing to say about why. Prefer `unavailable` with a reason: a disabled button can't be focused, so its reason can't be heard.

props.name: unavailable
props.description: The action can't happen now, and why, e.g. "Add a title first". The button stays focusable, keeps its contrast, does nothing when pressed and says why as its description and tooltip.

props.name: type
props.description: `submit` only inside a form.

props.name: size
props.description: xs 24, s 36, normal 44, m 48, l 56, xl 64, xxl 80 px high. `xs` and `s` are dense sizes (written exceptions to the 44 px target); `normal` everywhere else.

props.name: progress
props.description: How an operation in progress shows: `inside` (a spinner in place of the icon), `ring` (an arc around the border, the content kept) or `fill` (the button fills up from its start edge as `value` grows). `fill` needs a known `value` and a `primary` or `danger` button with a label at least `c.button.fill-min-inline` wide; otherwise it shows `inside` (and warns in development).

props.name: value
props.description: How far the operation in progress is, 0 to 100, from a real total (bytes, items, steps). Only for `progress="fill"`; leave it out when the total isn't known.

props.name: expanded
props.description: For a disclosure: whether the region it opens is shown. Shown as a selected tint while true.

props.name: controls
props.description: For a disclosure: the id of the region it opens.

props.name: pressed
props.description: A toggle button (Q121): on or off, announced as pressed (`aria-pressed`), shown with `c.button.pressed-fill`. Switch is the default for a binary setting; use this only with a written reason in a `toggle-button:` comment just above it where it's used (a dense toolbar or a list row's eye and lock). Pair it with an icon that shows the state.

props.name: onPointerEnter
props.description: The pointer arrives over it (IP9), e.g. to preview what it opens. Runs beside the button's own hint handling.

props.name: onPointerLeave
props.description: The pointer leaves it (IP9).

props.name: onFocus
props.description: It takes focus (IP9).

props.name: onBlur
props.description: It loses focus (IP9).

props.name: onClick
props.description: An action with no saved result to confirm (open, close, cancel, retry, export).

props.name: busy
props.description: The action it started is still running elsewhere (an export, a sync): shows in progress and ignores presses until false.

props.name: pendingLabel
props.description: Present tense while `busy`, e.g. "Exporting…"; the label stays when left out.

props.name: onCommit
props.description: Saves something: the button shows pending, then confirmed, on itself. Reject the promise when it fails.

props.name: pendingLabel
props.description: Present tense while pending, e.g. "Saving…".

props.name: doneLabel
props.description: Past tense once stored, e.g. "Saved".

props.name: onError
props.description: The failure, for the scope the button acts on (its section's message bar). The button itself returns to rest.

props.name: href
props.description: Goes somewhere (IP8): the button is a link (`a[href]`) that looks like a button, for the few places a destination is the main call to action (a hero's "Get tickets", a header's "Sign up"). Everywhere else a destination is a Link. No progress, commit or disclosure: `type`, `progress`, `value`, `expanded` and `controls` don't apply.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Runs as it's followed, e.g. a router taking over: call `event.preventDefault()` to stop the browser's own navigation.
